extracted.intended_audience: investigators preparing NIH (NIAID) R01 (PA-13-302) grant applications / institutional grant administrators
extracted.subtask_description: A filled sample NIH/NIAID R01 (PA-13-302) application demonstrating required forms, attachment sections, and content expectations (Project Summary, Narrative, Specific Aims, Facilities, Equipment, Biosketches, Resource Sharing, Vertebrate Animals, etc.). Useful as a template for preparing/resubmitting an R01 application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow FOA/application-format instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly instructs applicants to follow the FOA's instructions (e.g., PA-13-302). It links to NIAID sample applications and warns that sample applications may not reflect the latest format or rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete and accurate SF424 (R&R) and required signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: The SF424 (R&R) form must be completed (type of submission, applicant information, federal identifier, dates, applicant contact info) and signed by the authorized institutional representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fields shown include Type of Submission, Applicant Information, Organizational DUNS/EIN/TIN, Project/Performance Site location, Authorized Representative signature and date. The applicant certifies that statements are true/complete and agrees to required assurances; false statements may lead to penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide Project Summary/Abstract with hypothesis, aims, rationale, significance, innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Project Summary/Abstract must state the long-term goal, objective, central hypothesis, rationale, and specific aims of the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample language demonstrates the required elements: long-term goal, objective of the grant, central hypothesis, rationale, and enumerated specific aims (e.g., Aim 1, Aim 2, Aim 3). The abstract should make clear expected contributions, significance to disease (IBD example), and innovation (novel mechanism or approach).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative: public health relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Project Narrative that explains the relevance of the proposed research to public health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample Project Narrative explains disease burden (IBD prevalence, remission rates), how expected findings will inform therapeutics or clinical trials, and the anticipated public health impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include Specific Aims and Research Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a Specific Aims page and a Research Strategy that lays out hypotheses, experimental aims, and the approach to test them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific Aims should be concise, numbered, and hypothesis-driven. Research Strategy should expand on aims with background, significance, innovation, and approach details (methodology, expected outcomes, and how results will be interpreted).

rubrics_metrics.name: BIOGRAPHICAL SKETCH format and page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a biographical sketch for senior/key personnel and other significant contributors following the prescribed format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction: 'Provide the following information for the Senior/key personnel and other significant contributors. Follow this format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.' Include: name, eRA Commons user name, position title, education/training (begin with baccalaureate), personal statement, positions and honors, contributions to science, and ongoing/previous research support as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & Related Senior/Key Person Profile completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete expanded profiles for the PD/PI and all senior/key persons, including role, degree, organization, contact info, and attachments (biosketch, current & pending support).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample shows required fields (position/title, organization, degree type, project role) and that files (biosketch, current & pending support) must be attached for each named person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects section: declare involvement and provide IRB status
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly indicate whether human subjects are involved and, if yes, whether the project is exempt or requires IRB review; provide IRB approval status and Human Subject Assurance number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form questions require: Are Human Subjects Involved? If YES: Is the project exempt? If not exempt, is IRB review pending? Provide exemption number if applicable or IRB approval date and assurance number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals section: declare use and provide IACUC status
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether vertebrate animals are used and, if yes, provide IACUC review status, IACUC approval date (or indicate pending), and Animal Welfare Assurance Number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form specifically asks: Are Vertebrate Animals Used? If Yes: Is the IACUC review pending? Provide IACUC approval date and Animal Welfare Assurance Number (sample A3291-01 shown).

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources description
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe institutional facilities, cores, shared resources, and relevant personnel that will support the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample lists cores (e.g., Medical Genome Facility components), facility directors, shared resources (sequencing, imaging, proteomics), and key personnel. The description should demonstrate that the institutional environment is adequate to perform the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment listing and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: List major equipment available to the project/laboratory (e.g., PCR machines, real-time PCR, confocal microscope, FACS) and their capacities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample enumerates specific items and counts (5 conventional PCR machines, 2 real time PCR, Zeiss confocal, BD LSR II FACS, tissue culture incubators, -80°C freezers, computational resources). Show that needed instrumentation is accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plan and public access compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a Resource Sharing Plan describing how data and model organisms will be shared and comply with NIH public access policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample commitments: deposit peer-reviewed publications into PubMed Central within 12 months, make cell and mouse lines available upon request pursuant to institutional and NIH guidelines. Follow NIH Public Access Policies for data and publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support content and commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide Letters of Support from collaborators/core directors that describe the nature of collaboration, available expertise, resources/cores, and concrete commitments (e.g., provision of mouse lines, technical assistance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample letters explicitly state available capabilities (CRISPR/TALEN assistance, mouse lines, blinded histologic scoring assay), willingness to collaborate, and resources to be provided. Letters should demonstrate feasibility and institutional/collegial support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and associated attachments (Modular Budget, Personnel Justification, Current & Pending Support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide estimated project funding details, required budget forms (PHS 398 Modular Budget if applicable), personnel justification, and attach Current & Pending Support for senior/key personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form fields include total federal funds requested, total non-federal funds, total combined funds, and estimated program income. Attach budget files and justifications as listed in the Table of Contents (PHS 398 Modular Budget, Personnel Justification, Current & Pending Support files).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications, assurances, and truthfulness attestation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authorized Organizational Representative (and signers) must certify compliance with listed certifications and assurances and attest to the truthfulness and accuracy of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By signing, the authorized representative certifies the statements contained in the list of certifications and assurances (or indicates where to find them) and acknowledges penalties for false statements. The application includes a check/affirmation: 'I agree*'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative/other required attachments (Table of Contents entries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include all administrative and required attachments listed in the Table of Contents (Performance Sites, Project Summary/Abstract, Project Narrative, Facilities & Other Resources, Equipment, Senior/Key Person, PHS398 Cover Page Supplement, PHS 398 Modular Budget, Personnel Justification, PHS 398 Research Plan, Introduction (if resubmission), Specific Aims, Research Strategy, Progress Report/Publications List, Vertebrate Animals, Bibliography & References Cited, Letters of Support, Resource Sharing Plans).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample's Table of Contents enumerates required attachments and their order. Ensure all listed items are present, properly named, and paginated as required by the FOA and application instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of proprietary/privileged information and project impact questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer whether proprietary/privileged information is included, whether the project has an environmental impact, whether the performance site is a historic place, and whether the project involves international activities/collaborators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form checkboxes require Yes/No responses and explanations when applicable (e.g., if project impacts the environment, provide explanation; if international partners involved, identify countries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright, FOIA, and data confidentiality notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware that the text is copyrighted and that NIH/NIAID will respond to FOIA requests subject to exemptions and redactions to protect confidential commercial/financial information, reviewer comments and deliberations, and personal privacy information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample states the awardee provided permission for NIAID to post the application for nonprofit educational use under specific conditions. Applicants should understand how FOIA and copyright interact with posted application materials.
